questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook tasty meals with leftovers from the fridge
Why supermarkets in Europe are becoming too expensive
Food waste and how one woman helped cut it in Denmark
Food shortages in Russia and how people survived them
questions.why: Dan and Neil discuss food waste and Selina Juul's campaign that helped Denmark cut its waste.

questions.q: What does Neil do at the start of the programme?
options: Throws away part of an apple he couldn't finish
Eats someone else's leftovers from the fridge
Brings a big lunch into the studio to share
Recycles his food waste in a special bin
questions.why: Neil threw away the rest of his apple because it was big and he couldn't finish it.

questions.q: According to Dan, where does most of Europe's food waste come from?
options: Restaurants
Supermarkets
Farms
People's homes
questions.why: Dan says 53% of food waste in Europe comes from households.

questions.q: What usually happens to this wasted food?
options: It is recycled into animal food
It goes into landfill and rots
It is given to hungry people
It is burnt for energy
questions.why: Dan says it goes into landfills and decays, causing greenhouse gases.

options: It has stopped all food waste
It has cut its food waste by 25%
It has cut food prices by 25%
It has built new landfills
questions.why: Dan says Denmark has managed to reduce its food waste by 25%.

questions.q: Why was Selina Juul shocked when she moved to Denmark?
options: The supermarkets had very little food on the shelves
Food was much more expensive there than it was in Moscow
Nobody cooked at home and everyone ate in restaurants
She grew up with food shortages and saw lots of food wasted
questions.why: She grew up in Moscow unsure of getting food, then was shocked to see so much wasted in Denmark.

questions.q: How did Selina Juul start her campaign?
options: By writing to the government
By opening a restaurant
By starting a Facebook page in 2008
By appearing on TV
questions.why: Dan says she started a Facebook page called 'stop wasting food' in 2008.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Selina Juul's ideas?
options: Making supermarkets pay a tax on waste
Getting supermarkets to stop selling in bulk
Writing a cookbook for leftovers
Setting up education programmes in schools
questions.why: Dan mentions stopping bulk selling, a leftovers cookbook and school programmes, but not a tax.
